sentences.text:
OFFICE NO. NOTE 10. 07.05.2025 Dr.VJP, J  I.A.No.1 of 2024  The instant petition under Section 389(1)
 of Cr.P.C has been filed by the  Petitioner/Accused No.1 seeking to release him  on bail by suspending the sentence imposed  against him, pending disposal of the criminal  appeal.

The Petitioner is convicted and  sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for  twenty years and to pay fine of Rs.25,000/- IDSI  for six months for the offence under Section  376-D IPC in Sessions Case No.132 of 2020 on  the file of the Court of Special Judge for Speedy  trial offenecs under POCSO Act, Vijayawada  vide judgment dated 29.07.2024.
 Heard Sri Challa Ajay Kumar,
learned  counsel for the Petitioner and Ms.K.Priyanka  Lakshmi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor  for Respondent.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner would submit that, Accused and the victim both are elders and that the Petitioner was acquitted for the offence under POCSO Act.
Learned counsel would further submit that they have good grounds to succeed in the appeal and the appeal may take considerable time for disposal.

Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the petition and would submit that the Petitioner is the main culprit in the alleged offence and that and the acquittal before the Juvenile Justice Board is not on merits and is based on the settlement before SL. DATE ORDER OFFICE NO.
NOTE the elders.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

Considering the submissions, in view of the nature of the offences, and as no case for suspension is made out, this Court is not inclined to suspend the sentence of imprisonment imposed against the Petitioner and hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
